title: Google Workspace connector
description: The second major identity platform, built against the connector guide to prove the abstraction holds.
acceptance: Admin SDK Reports API consent flow with read-only scopes
Login, admin, Drive, Gmail and token audit activities are collected
OCSF normalisation produces output equivalent to M365 for comparable events
Required no change to ingest, detection or correlation
Existing rules fire correctly on Google events without modification where the technique applies

tests.desc: Consent flow and collection succeed against a Google test tenant
Equivalent sign-in events from Google and Microsoft normalise to the same OCSF shape
Impossible travel fires correctly on Google sign-in data
Cursor and checkpoint semantics survive a restart

title: AWS CloudTrail connector
description: Push-based ingest via EventBridge and SQS — the lowest-latency source and the first non-polling connector.
acceptance: Cross-account role assumption with an external id, documented for the customer
SQS consumption with correct visibility timeout and deletion semantics
CloudTrail events normalise to OCSF
The push path coexists with polling connectors without special-casing downstream
Message loss is impossible — deletion occurs only after durable write

tests.desc: Role assumption and consumption succeed against a test account
A consumer crash before deletion results in redelivery, not loss
CloudTrail normalisation matches golden fixtures

title: Azure and Entra ID connector
description: Diagnostic settings to Event Hub for Azure activity and Entra ID sign-in logs beyond what the M365 connector covers.
acceptance: Event Hub consumption with checkpointing
Entra ID risk detections and conditional access results are captured
Normalises to OCSF consistently with the M365 connector
Customer configuration is documented with screenshots
Overlap with M365-sourced events is deduplicated

tests.desc: Event Hub consumption with checkpoint recovery after restart
Deduplication against M365-sourced equivalents is correct
Risk detections surface as signals

title: Hot-tenant sharding activation
description: Activate the shard split designed for in P1 and P3, so a single large tenant can no longer pin a partition.
acceptance: Tenants exceeding a configured EPS threshold are automatically re-keyed across shards
Correlation merges windows across shards correctly
Shard assignment changes do not split an open case
The threshold is configurable and changes take effect without redeployment
Sharded and unsharded tenants behave identically from the product's perspective

tests.desc: A tenant crossing the threshold is sharded automatically
An open case is not split by a shard assignment change
A single tenant at 10k EPS does not increase other tenants' lag
Un-sharding a tenant that falls below threshold is safe

title: ClickHouse cold tiering and retention enforcement
description: Age partitions beyond 90 days to object storage, enforce per-plan retention, and keep queries working transparently across tiers.
acceptance: Storage policy moves aged partitions to S3 automatically
Queries spanning hot and cold return correct results with only a latency difference
Retention is enforced per plan tier and deletion is verifiable
Cold-tier query latency is documented and surfaced in the UI as a slower path
Storage cost per tenant is measured against the cost model

tests.desc: An aged partition moves to cold storage and remains queryable
A query spanning both tiers returns a complete result set
Retention deletion removes data and is verifiable

title: Production Kubernetes deployment and Terraform infrastructure
description: Everything that has run in Docker Compose now runs as declared, reproducible production infrastructure.
acceptance: All infrastructure is declared in Terraform; no manual console changes
Services deploy via Kubernetes manifests with resource limits and health probes
Horizontal autoscaling is configured against meaningful metrics, not just CPU
Secrets come from a secret manager, never from environment files in the repo
A full environment can be rebuilt from scratch in under two hours, and this has been done

tests.desc: Terraform apply builds a complete environment from nothing
Pod failure is recovered automatically without data loss
Autoscaling responds correctly to a load spike
A disaster-recovery rebuild is performed and timed

title: Full-scale load test at 30k EPS
description: The P7 exit criterion: the whole pipeline, not just detection, sustaining peak load with the alert latency SLO intact.
acceptance: 30,000 EPS sustained for one hour across the complete pipeline
p95 critical alert latency stays under 3 minutes throughout
No unbounded queue growth anywhere in the pipeline
Cost at this load is measured and compared against the model
Results are published and a regression gate is established

tests.desc: 30k EPS sustained for one hour end to end
p95 alert latency under 3 minutes at peak
No queue in the pipeline grows unboundedly
Measured cost at load is within 20% of the model

title: SOC 2 Type I evidence collection
description: The certification larger customers and MSP procurement require before signing.
acceptance: Control mapping is documented against the trust services criteria
Access reviews, change management and incident response procedures are written and followed
Evidence collection is automated where possible rather than assembled manually
A gap assessment is completed and remediation tracked to closure
Policies are approved and acknowledged by everyone with production access

tests.desc: Gap assessment completed with every finding tracked
Automated evidence collection runs and produces the expected artefacts
Access review is executed end to end

title: Backup, restore and disaster recovery verification
description: A backup that has never been restored is not a backup. RPO and RTO are stated, tested and evidenced.
acceptance: Postgres and ClickHouse backups run on schedule with monitored success
RPO and RTO targets are stated per data store and justified
A full restore is performed and timed at least quarterly
The audit chain verifies after a restore
The procedure is documented well enough for someone who did not write it

tests.desc: A full Postgres restore completes within the stated RTO
A ClickHouse restore completes and data reconciles
Audit chain verification passes after restore
An engineer who did not write the runbook executes the restore successfully

title: Customer-authored detection rules [cuttable]
description: A sandboxed path for customer-written rules. ADR-0004 says this supersedes rather than bends the compiled-rule decision, so it needs its own ADR first.
acceptance: A new ADR is written superseding the relevant part of ADR-0004
Customer rules execute in a resource-limited sandbox with a hard timeout
A customer rule cannot degrade platform performance for other tenants
Rules are validated and tested against fixtures before activation
Customer rules are scoped strictly to the authoring tenant

tests.desc: A pathological customer rule is terminated at its resource limit
A customer rule cannot read another tenant's events
Customer rules do not affect platform-wide evaluation latency
A rule failing its own fixtures cannot be activated

title: Multi-region readiness [cuttable]
description: Data residency for customers who require it, and reduced latency for distant regions. Cut unless a contract requires it.
acceptance: Tenant data residency is selectable at provisioning and enforced thereafter
Regional isolation is verified — no tenant data crosses its assigned region
The control plane operates across regions without becoming a single point of failure
Cross-region failover is documented and tested
Cost impact is measured per region

tests.desc: Tenant data never leaves its assigned region, verified at the storage layer
Cross-region failover completes within the stated RTO
Control plane survives the loss of one region
